title: introduce-invocation-cohort-analyzer-and-token-latency-correlation-heatmap
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: operators increasingly need to understand why small fractions of invocations cause large cost and latency deviations. This PR adds an Invocation Cohort Analyzer that groups invocations by runtime signals (prompt length, model variant, route, kernel path) and exposes cohort-level rollups plus a cross-correlation heatmap between token position and per-token latency. What this change does: adds a lightweight cohort-aggregation pipeline in observability-service, a new metric name invocation.cohort.latency_ms (histogram buckets tuned for 1-2000ms), a token_latency_heatmap gauge exported as per-invocation sparse bins, Grafana dashboard panels for cohort timeline, cohort compare, and token-position latency heatmap, and an alert tuning recipe for long-tail latency spikes that uses cohort-aware baselines and an adaptive smoothing factor. Backfill: a migration/backfill script (observability/scripts/backfill_cohorts.py) performs a 30-day coarse cohort rollup to seed baselines. Telemetry cost: adds ~0.5% to telemetry ingestion at peak, optimized with batched export and reservoir sampling of full invocation traces. Rollout plan: staged toggle behind feature flag observability.cohort_analyzer.enabled with canary in us-west-2 for 48 hours, followed by global rollout if no regressions. Related: ENG-4219 (cohort design), ENG-4280 (alerting baseline integration).
commits: initial cohort analyzer service and API surface
add histogram metric and bucket config
implement token-latency heatmap exporter and sampling
add grafana dashboard JSON and panels
fix flaky unit tests and CI lint issues
review_comments: Lina Ortiz: Can we ensure the bucket boundaries align with existing kernel-level histograms? Otherwise percentiles will be misleading.
Maya Chen: Bucket boundaries aligned and documented in observability/metrics/registry.py; added a conversion helper for comparisons.
Noah Patel: Alert tuning looks promising but we should gate it behind a stabilization window to avoid alert storms during rollout.
Maya Chen: Added a 1-hour mute window per cohort during backfill and feature-flagged rollout; documented in PR checklist.
Rajat Singh: Unit tests are failing intermittently in CI; looks like a time-dependent assertion in test_cohort_analyzer.py.
Maya Chen: Reworked tests to use deterministic clock and added a retry-friendly assertion for async export.
release_notes: Add Invocation Cohort Analyzer: cohort rollups, token-position latency heatmap, Grafana dashboard panels, and cohort-aware long-tail latency alerting. Backfill included for 30 days of historical baselines.
notes_for_ops: Feature is behind observability.cohort_analyzer.enabled. Canary in us-west-2 only for first 48 hours. Watch craft: invocation.cohort.latency_ms histogram and token_latency_heatmap gauge for ingestion spikes. Backfill will add temporary burst; monitor telemetry ingestion and alert on >3% metric queue growth.
manual_steps: 1) Enable feature flag in infra/feature_flags.yaml for a single region. 2) Run backfill: python observability/scripts/backfill_cohorts.py --start 2025-12-10 --end 2026-02-10 --coarse. 3) Monitor ci/observability-dashboard panels and mute policy for 1 hour per cohort during ramp.
qa_notes: Added deterministic test harness for cohort aggregation. QA should validate cohort boundaries by creating synthetic invocations with controlled token positions and verifying heatmap intensity matches expected latency distributions. Verify alert suppression during initial backfill window.
mitigations: 1) Feature flag gating and region canary. 2) Backfill runs in controlled batches with rate limit. 3) Sampling reduces payloads; full-trace export only on sampled invocations.
additional_context: This PR is intended to reduce MTTR for long-tail latency issues and provide operators a lens to quickly identify whether spikes are driven by prompt shapes, specific models, kernel paths, or tenant-level traffic patterns. Will follow up with a short runbook and a playbook for common cohort-driven incidents.
